stories: Ada Lovelace published notes describing an algorithm for Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine, often called the first computer program.
Engineers at Bell Labs built the first working transistor, the building block of every modern chip.
ARPANET, the network that grew into the internet, sent its first message between two US universities.
Intel released the 4004, the first commercially available microprocessor.
Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web while working at CERN.
Linus Torvalds announced Linux as a hobby project. It now runs most of the world’s servers.
Google was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
Git was created by Linus Torvalds to manage Linux development.
The first iPhone went on sale and changed what people expect from a phone.
A deep neural network called AlexNet won the ImageNet challenge by a wide margin and sparked the modern AI boom.
The internet switched to TCP/IP, the protocols it still uses today.
Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email and chose the @ sign for addresses.
